/-!
# Rectilinear crossing number and halving lines

A *rectilinear drawing* of the complete graph $K_n$ is given by a set $S$ of $n$ points in
general position in the plane (no three collinear); its edges are the straight line segments
joining the points of $S$. The number of crossings of this drawing is denoted $\overline{cr}(S)$,
and the *rectilinear crossing number* $\overline{cr}(n)$ of $K_n$ is the minimum of
$\overline{cr}(S)$ over all such $S$.

A *halving line* of $S$ is a line which passes through two points of $S$ and equally bisects the
remaining points.

Conjecture: for each arrangement of points in which $\overline{cr}(n)$ is minimized, the number
of halving lines is maximized. The converse is known to be false.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Crossing number (graph theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/crossing_number_%28graph_theory%29)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [Rectilinear Crossing Number project](http://www.ist.tugraz.at/staff/aichholzer/research/rp/triangulations/crossing/)
-/

blocks.name: crossings
blocks.text:
/-- The number of crossings $\overline{cr}(S)$ of the rectilinear drawing of the complete graph
on the point set `S`: the number of unordered pairs of edges `s(a, b)`, `s(c, d)` with four
distinct endpoints in `S` whose interiors (open segments) meet. -/
noncomputable def crossings (S : Finset ℝ²) : ℕ :=
  {e : Sym2 (Sym2 ℝ²) | ∃ a ∈ S, ∃ b ∈ S, ∃ c ∈ S, ∃ d ∈ S,
    e = s(s(a, b), s(c, d)) ∧ ({a, b, c, d} : Finset ℝ²).card = 4 ∧
      (openSegment ℝ a b ∩ openSegment ℝ c d).Nonempty}.ncard

blocks.docstring:
The line `ℓ` is a *halving line* of `S`: it passes through two distinct points `a, b` of `S`,
and the two open half-planes bounded by `ℓ` contain the same number of points of `S`.
The side of `ℓ` on which a point `p` lies is recorded by the sign of the oriented angle
`∡ a b p`, which is `0` exactly when `p` lies on `ℓ`.

For `S` in general position (no three collinear) the only points of `S` on `ℓ` are `a` and `b`,
so `ℓ` equally bisects the remaining `#S - 2` points.

justification.closest_existing_considered: AffineSubspace.SSameSide/SOppSide and EuclideanGeometry.oangle sign (used as primitives); no existing halving-line or k-set definition.
justification.name: CrossingNumber.IsHalvingLine
justification.why_needed: Halving lines of a planar point set are not defined anywhere in Mathlib or the repository.

blocks.name: IsHalvingLine
blocks.text:
/-- The line `ℓ` is a *halving line* of `S`: it passes through two distinct points `a, b` of `S`,
and the two open half-planes bounded by `ℓ` contain the same number of points of `S`.
The side of `ℓ` on which a point `p` lies is recorded by the sign of the oriented angle
`∡ a b p`, which is `0` exactly when `p` lies on `ℓ`.

For `S` in general position (no three collinear) the only points of `S` on `ℓ` are `a` and `b`,
so `ℓ` equally bisects the remaining `#S - 2` points. -/
def IsHalvingLine (S : Finset ℝ²) (ℓ : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ a ∈ S, ∃ b ∈ S, a ≠ b ∧ ℓ = line[ℝ, a, b] ∧
    #{p ∈ S | (∡ a b p).sign = 1} = #{p ∈ S | (∡ a b p).sign = -1}

blocks.code:
noncomputable def halvingLines (S : Finset ℝ²) : ℕ :=
  {ℓ | IsHalvingLine S ℓ}.ncard
blocks.docstring: The number of halving lines of the point set `S`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Set.ncard applied to the bespoke predicate; no existing counting definition.
justification.name: CrossingNumber.halvingLines
justification.why_needed: Cardinality of the set of halving lines, needed to compare arrangements.

blocks.text:
/-- The number of halving lines of the point set `S`. -/
noncomputable def halvingLines (S : Finset ℝ²) : ℕ :=
  {ℓ | IsHalvingLine S ℓ}.ncard

@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem crossing_number : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ S : Finset ℝ², NonTrilinear (S : Set ℝ²) →
      (∀ T : Finset ℝ², #T = #S → NonTrilinear (T : Set ℝ²) →
        crossings S ≤ crossings T) →
      ∀ T : Finset ℝ², #T = #S → NonTrilinear (T : Set ℝ²) →
        halvingLines T ≤ halvingLines S := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
For each arrangement of points in which the rectilinear crossing number is minimized, is the
number of halving lines maximized?

Precisely: let $S$ be a set of $n$ points in general position (no three collinear) in the plane
such that $\overline{cr}(S) = \overline{cr}(n)$, i.e. the straight-line drawing of $K_n$ on $S$
has the minimum number of crossings among all $n$-point sets in general position. Is the number
of halving lines of $S$ then the maximum number of halving lines of an $n$-point set in general
position?

The question is asked for every $n$. For odd $n$ no line through two points of a set in general
position equally bisects the remaining $n - 2$ points, so the statement is trivially true in that
case; the content of the conjecture is for even $n$.

  sorry

@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem crossings_eq_zero_of_card_lt {S : Finset ℝ²} (h : #S < 4) : crossings S = 0 := by
  rw [crossings]
  convert Set.ncard_empty (Sym2 (Sym2 ℝ²)) using 2
  ext e
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false, not_exists, not_and]
  rintro a ha b hb c hc d hd - hcard -
  have hsub : ({a, b, c, d} : Finset ℝ²) ⊆ S := by
    intro x hx
    simp only [mem_insert, mem_singleton] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> assumption
  have := card_le_card hsub
  omega

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no conjecture (article asserts the positive answer as the conjecture): for every n and every n-point set S in general position (no three collinear) whose straight-line drawing of K_n has the minimum number of crossings among all such n-point sets, the number of halving lines of S (lines through 2 points of S with (n-2)/2 remaining points on each side) equals the maximum halving-line count over all n-point sets in general position; implicit quantifier over all n, the general-position hypothesis is implicit, and for odd n the halving-line count is 0 under the literal 'equally bisects' definition so the claim is vacuous there (some sources restrict to even n); the article's remark that the converse fails is background, not a posed question.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same proposition (∀ S in general position [NonTrilinear] that minimizes the straight-line K_n crossing count among all general-position sets of the same size, S maximizes the halving-line count among those sets), wrapped as `answer(sorry) ↔ P` so answer(True) is the positive conjecture. All compiled cleanly and none had a faithfulness defect. c05 was chosen because its crossing count is the literal definition (unordered pairs of edges with four distinct endpoints whose open segments meet, no reliance on the convex-position characterisation), halving lines are counted literally as lines (affine subspaces), sides are detected via the sign of `∡ a b p` (0 exactly on the line), extrema are stated relationally (no sInf/sSup defaults), it has proven boundary tests, precise docstrings, and no global `open Classical` (c08 violates that rule; c03 ships a `sorry` test; c02/c07/c08 use the convex-quadrilateral characterisation; c01 packages hypotheses into extra predicates). My only edits were reflowing two over-long lines.

context:
In graph theory, the crossing number cr(G) of a graph G is the lowest number of edge crossings of a plane drawing of the graph G. For instance, a graph is planar if and only if its crossing number is zero. Determining the crossing number continues to be of great importance in graph drawing, as user studies have shown that drawing graphs with few crossings makes it easier for people to understand the drawing.
The study of crossing numbers originated in Turán's brick factory problem, in which Pál Turán asked for a factory plan that minimized the number of crossings between tracks connecting brick kilns to storage sites. Mathematically, this problem can be formalized as asking for the crossing number of a complete bipartite graph. The same problem arose independently in sociology at approximately the same time, in connection with the construction of sociograms. Turán's conjectured formula for the crossing numbers of complete bipartite graphs remains unproven, as does an analogous formula for the complete graphs.
The crossing number inequality states that, for graphs where the number e of edges is sufficiently larger than the number n of vertices, the crossing number is at least proportional to e3/n2. It has applications in VLSI design and incidence geometry.
Without further qualification, the crossing number allows drawings in which the edges may be represented by arbitrary curves. A variation of this concept, the rectilinear crossing number, requires all edges to be straight li

decomposition_objections.text: None. One minor remark: the note says the claim is 'vacuous' for odd n; more precisely it is trivially true there (all halving-line counts are 0, so the conclusion 0 ≤ 0 holds), which is consistent with quantifying over all n.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Rectilinear crossing number and halving lines

A *rectilinear drawing* of the complete graph $K_n$ is given by a set $S$ of $n$ points in

joining the points of $S$. The number of crossings of this drawing is denoted $\overline{cr}(S)$,

remaining points.

Conjecture: for each arrangement of points in which $\overline{cr}(n)$ is minimized, the number
of halving lines is maximized. The converse is known to be false.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Crossing number (graph theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/crossing_number_%28graph_theory%29)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [Rectilinear Crossing Number project](http://www.ist.tugraz.at/staff/aichholzer/research/rp/triangulations/crossing/)
-/

open EuclideanGeometry Finset

namespace CrossingNumber

/-- The number of crossings $\overline{cr}(S)$ of the rectilinear drawing of the complete graph
on the point set `S`: the number of unordered pairs of edges `s(a, b)`, `s(c, d)` with four
distinct endpoints in `S` whose interiors (open segments) meet. -/
noncomputable def crossings (S : Finset ℝ²) : ℕ :=
  {e : Sym2 (Sym2 ℝ²) | ∃ a ∈ S, ∃ b ∈ S, ∃ c ∈ S, ∃ d ∈ S,
    e = s(s(a, b), s(c, d)) ∧ ({a, b, c, d} : Finset ℝ²).card = 4 ∧
      (openSegment ℝ a b ∩ openSegment ℝ c d).Nonempty}.ncard

/-- The line `ℓ` is a *halving line* of `S`: it passes through two distinct points `a, b` of `S`,
and the two open half-planes bounded by `ℓ` contain the same number of points of `S`.
The side of `ℓ` on which a point `p` lies is recorded by the sign of the oriented angle
`∡ a b p`, which is `0` exactly when `p` lies on `ℓ`.

For `S` in general position (no three collinear) the only points of `S` on `ℓ` are `a` and `b`,
so `ℓ` equally bisects the remaining `#S - 2` points. -/
def IsHalvingLine (S : Finset ℝ²) (ℓ : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ a ∈ S, ∃ b ∈ S, a ≠ b ∧ ℓ = line[ℝ, a, b] ∧
    #{p ∈ S | (∡ a b p).sign = 1} = #{p ∈ S | (∡ a b p).sign = -1}

/-- The number of halving lines of the point set `S`. -/
noncomputable def halvingLines (S : Finset ℝ²) : ℕ :=
  {ℓ | IsHalvingLine S ℓ}.ncard

/--
For each arrangement of points in which the rectilinear crossing number is minimized, is the
number of halving lines maximized?

Precisely: let $S$ be a set of $n$ points in general position (no three collinear) in the plane
such that $\overline{cr}(S) = \overline{cr}(n)$, i.e. the straight-line drawing of $K_n$ on $S$
has the minimum number of crossings among all $n$-point sets in general position. Is the number
of halving lines of $S$ then the maximum number of halving lines of an $n$-point set in general
position?

The question is asked for every $n$. For odd $n$ no line through two points of a set in general
position equally bisects the remaining $n - 2$ points, so the statement is trivially true in that
case; the content of the conjecture is for even $n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem crossing_number : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ S : Finset ℝ², NonTrilinear (S : Set ℝ²) →
      (∀ T : Finset ℝ², #T = #S → NonTrilinear (T : Set ℝ²) →
        crossings S ≤ crossings T) →
      ∀ T : Finset ℝ², #T = #S → NonTrilinear (T : Set ℝ²) →
        halvingLines T ≤ halvingLines S := by
  sorry

/-- A drawing with fewer than four vertices has no crossings. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem crossings_eq_zero_of_card_lt {S : Finset ℝ²} (h : #S < 4) : crossings S = 0 := by
  rw [crossings]
  convert Set.ncard_empty (Sym2 (Sym2 ℝ²)) using 2
  ext e
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false, not_exists, not_and]
  rintro a ha b hb c hc d hd - hcard -
  have hsub : ({a, b, c, d} : Finset ℝ²) ⊆ S := by
    intro x hx
    simp only [mem_insert, mem_singleton] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> assumption
  have := card_le_card hsub
  omega

/-- A set with fewer than two points has no halving lines. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem halvingLines_eq_zero_of_card_lt {S : Finset ℝ²} (h : #S < 2) : halvingLines S = 0 := by
  rw [halvingLines]
  convert Set.ncard_empty (AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ²) using 2
  ext ℓ
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false, IsHalvingLine, not_exists,
    not_and]
  rintro a ha b hb hab - -
  have hsub : ({a, b} : Finset ℝ²) ⊆ S := by
    intro x hx
    simp only [mem_insert, mem_singleton] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl <;> assumption
  have := card_le_card hsub
  rw [card_pair hab] at this
  omega

end CrossingNumber

items: General position is taken as 'no three collinear' (`EuclideanGeometry.NonTrilinear` from FormalConjecturesForMathlib) and is imposed both on the arrangement S and on all competitors T; this is the standard domain of rectilinear drawings of K_n (Aichholzer et al. / Rectilinear Crossing Number project) and matches the decomposition note.

The minimization/maximization is expressed directly as comparisons against every T with `#T = #S` (rather than via `sInf`/`sSup` definitions of cr̄(n) and the maximum halving-line count) to avoid default-value pitfalls; the two formulations are equivalent.

`crossings S` counts unordered pairs of edges `s(a,b)`, `s(c,d)` with four pairwise distinct endpoints whose open segments meet (elements of `Sym2 (Sym2 ℝ²)`). In general position this is exactly the number of crossings of the straight-line drawing (adjacent edges cannot cross, closed vs. open segments coincide). Distinctness of endpoints is required explicitly so the definition does not depend on general position for degenerate cases.

`IsHalvingLine S ℓ` requires ℓ = line through two distinct points a, b ∈ S with equally many points of S in each open half-plane; sides are encoded by `(∡ a b p).sign = 1` vs `= -1` (sign 0 ⇔ p on the line, by `oangle_sign_eq_zero_iff_collinear`; sign constant on a side and negated across sides by `SSameSide.oangle_sign_eq`/`SOppSide.oangle_sign_eq_neg`). Under the general-position hypothesis the only points of S on ℓ are a and b, so this is exactly 'equally bisects the remaining n-2 points' with (n-2)/2 on each side. The count is of lines (`AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ²`), which in general position equals the count of point pairs.

Quantification is over all n (implicit in the statement), following the decomposition note. For odd n every general-position set has 0 halving lines under the literal 'equally bisects' definition, so the statement is trivially true there; the docstring records this. The question form of the list entry is rendered as `answer(sorry) ↔ P`, where `answer(True)` is the positive conjecture asserted by the article.
Two `@[category test]` lemmas with short proofs are included as basic API for the new definitions (no crossings with < 4 points; no halving lines with < 2 points).

reviewer_notes: Statement is a yes/no list entry; the article asserts the positive answer as the conjecture, so `answer(True)` = conjecture holds. Modeling decisions shared by all candidates and accepted: point sets are `Finset ℝ²`; general position = no three collinear (`EuclideanGeometry.NonTrilinear`), imposed on both S and competitors (standard domain of rectilinear drawings of K_n and of halving lines); implicit quantification over all n via `#T = #S`; odd n makes the conclusion trivially true (all halving-line counts 0), which is harmless. Boundary cases checked: n ≤ 3 trivial; n = 4 sanity check consistent (non-convex 4-sets have 0 crossings and 3 halving lines, convex ones 1 crossing and 2 halving lines). The counted sets are finite so `Set.ncard` has no default-value issue. The article's remark that the converse fails is background only and is mentioned in the module docstring, not formalized. Final file compiles with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning; lines over 100 chars are only URLs.

title: Rectilinear crossing number and halving lines
